headline: South Asia: Elon Musk calls on Zelensky to 'go' as Ukraine leader
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Elon Musk calls on Zelensky to 'go' as Ukraine leader.
- India: Missile heading towards Medina destroyed, says Saudi Arabia; Houthis deny attack.
- Persian Gulf Region: Ukrainians fear US intelligence cuts as Russian strikes intensify.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Disrupt, Strike, Assault and Endure: The 4 pillars of the US Army’s new warfare guidance.
- Military Times, 18 hours ago: Disrupt, Strike, Assault and Endure: The 4 pillars of the US Army’s new warfare guidance.
“How The Army Fights” is a new 46-page U.S. Army-issued guide on how the service should fight — and survive — on the modern battlefield.
- Military Times, 22 hours ago: US Army taps 9 companies to build next-gen command and control software.
The service announced contract awards worth $93.6 million across nine companies building applications for its Next Generation Command and Control software.
- Military Times, 21 hours ago: ‘You’re a coward’: Protesters heckle Hegseth during AUSA panel.
Protesters derailed a Washington, D.C., panel featuring Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Wednesday, calling him a “war criminal” and “Nazi.”
The Caribbean - bottom line: Reckoning over rights - Osborne challenges Chang’s stance on US deportation lawsuits, warns Jamaica could face scrutiny over rights safeguards.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: Reckoning over rights - Osborne challenges Chang’s stance on US deportation lawsuits, warns Jamaica could face scrutiny over rights safeguards.
National Security Minister Dr Horace Chang’s assertion that legal challenges in the United States (US) against its third-country deportation policy are of no concern to Jamaica has drawn criticism from civil society advocate Kay Osborne. Osborne described Chang’s statement as a “convenient deflection”, arguing that it sidesteps the Government’s responsibility to protect human rights under international law, including the obligation not to transfer people to places where they face torture or persecution.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Russians attack logistics company warehouses in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast.
Russian forces have attacked warehouses belonging to a logistics company in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast. Early reports indicate that no one was killed or injured.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Russian drone strikes near school in Poltava Oblast, children were in shelter.
A Russian drone has struck near a school in Poltava Oblast. The blast wave damaged the school's windows. The children and staff were in a shelter at the time of the strike and were unharmed.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Satellite image reveals damage at Borisoglebsk airfield after Ukrainian Neptune strike.
A satellite image shows damage at Russia's Borisoglebsk airfield after a Ukrainian Neptune missile strike on the night of 14-15 October.

- Balkan Insight, 8 hours ago: Black Sea Drone Attacks Expose Holes in Bulgarian Security Strategy.
Military experts are alarmed at what they see as inaction on the part of Bulgaria’s government in the face of spillover from Russia’s war in Ukraine.
- Balkan Insight, 5 hours ago: Albanian PM Blames Opposition After Another Night of Violent Clashes.
Edi Rama accuses opposition of trying to 'pull Albania down' after a second night of violence saw government buildings and businesses attacked and set on fire amid clashes between student protesters and police.
- Politico Europe, one hour ago: NATO allies to meet over Black Sea drone attacks on shipping.
The North Atlantic Council will discuss the crisis after series of attacks on cargo ships in the region, Romanian President Nicușor Dan tells POLITICO.
- Politico Europe, 5 hours ago: Croatia pumps the brakes on Montenegro’s EU membership bid.
Zagreb is pressing Podgorica to resolve long-standing disputes over war crimes, compensation and border demarcation before wrapping up EU accession talks.

A school roof collapsed in Peshawar, northwestern Pakistan, on Thursday 15 October, killing at least 32 pupils and a teacher. Officials said the roof was structurally weak and had been overloaded by construction work. The school’s owner was arrested and an investigation launched.

[New Zimbabwe] THE Zambezi River Authority (ZRA) has slashed water allocations for power generation at Kariba Dam to 23 billion cubic metres (BCM) in 2027, warning of a potentially dry season due to El Niño conditions.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Elon Musk calls on Zelensky to 'go' as Ukraine leader.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: Elon Musk calls on Zelensky to 'go' as Ukraine leader.
Tech billionaire Elon Musk called on Wednesday for Volodymyr Zelensky to “go” as Ukraine’s president, as Kyiv raised doubts over US support for the war-torn country. Ukraine accused the United States this week of helping Russia by failing to warn it of incoming missile strikes and hobbling Kyiv’s military response through changes to Musk’s satellite system which it uses for communications. “And so the slaughter continues,” Musk wrote on X.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Jerusalem Post, 5 hours ago: US considers hitting Iran with 'Mother of All Bombs': report.
The United States is considering using its biggest non-nuclear bomb against Iran if President Donald Trump should decide to renew combat in the war that has hit a deadlock, CNN reported on Thursday. The military is planning for the potential use of the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast (MOAB) bomb — better known by its nickname, the “Mother Of All Bombs” — to target Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites, according to the news outlet, which quoted officials familiar with the matter.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: IMF warns Gulf economies will not return to pre-war growth soon.
The International Monetary Fund expects energy-rich Middle Eastern economies to bounce back, but not in the medium term, the organisation’s regional chief said on Thursday, as fighting continued between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis. The statement comes as the IMF projects a widespread contraction in Gulf economies following months of war that began in Iran and has now spread to Saudi Arabia and Yemen, with maritime energy traffic still impacted.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: Palestinians fear violent olive harvest ahead of Israeli elections.
With a black eye and a bandage covering his face, Palestinian farmer Abdellatif Bazzari looks out at his rows of olive trees that are half harvested before the season has even started. Bazzari, who was injured in a raid on the fields by Israeli settlers that killed his cousin, is afraid to return to harvest the other half without some sort of army protection, fearing a new attack. Like many olive farmers in the plains nestled between the occupied West Bank’s sinuous limestone hills, Bazzari decided to harvest as early as possible this year, hoping both to save his crops and avoid beatings.
India - bottom line: Missile heading towards Medina destroyed, says Saudi Arabia; Houthis deny attack.
- Times of India - Top Stories, Jerusalem Post, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Missile heading towards Medina destroyed, says Saudi Arabia; Houthis deny attack.
A missile targeting Saudi Arabia's Medina region was intercepted by the Saudi-led coalition according to their spokesperson. Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree refuted this claim, stating no operations were conducted towards Saudi territories. The ongoing conflict has resulted in a series of airstrikes from both the Houthis and coalition forces. Recent incidents include the destruction of a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh by the coalition.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 12 hours ago: Nick Sirianni faces criticism: Why is Michael Vick asking Eagles fans for patience?.
Michael Vick has come forward to back Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni amidst mounting frustration from fans following a tough defeat to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Vick emphasizes the need for patience with both the coaching staff and quarterback Jalen Hurts, as rising tensions come from the offensive difficulties contributing to a three-game losing streak.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: ‘Where did you sell gold chains?’ New videos give big twist to Sharma murder case.
After Shraddha Dubey's confrontational videos with Shiva Sharma went viral, new footage emerged showing her demanding the return of jewelry she claims was stolen. The situation escalated following Shiva's fatal fall from an apartment building on October 9, prompting police to search for Shraddha and her associates while offering rewards for information. Investigators have yet to verify the authenticity of the videos or the surrounding events.

- South China Morning Post - China, 6 hours ago: Inside Nepal’s unending cycle of avalanches, floods and landslides.
Nepal has weathered three disasters in six weeks, including the deadly August flash flood, making this year one of the deadliest in a country where monsoon rains already frequently wreak havoc. Experts warn that climate change is only making matters worse. The rock-ice avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border that opened the floodgates in the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers on August 26 killed more than 1,450 people, with nearly 6,000 others still missing. - South China Morning Post - China, 5 hours ago: Cross-border matchmaking can lead to financial ruin, Chinese police warn rural men.
Authorities in the central Chinese province of Hunan have warned of the potential risks of cross-border arranged marriages, saying some relationships lack genuine emotional foundations and can lead to financial ruin or legal trouble. Marriages can be risky when they are organised by illegal matchmaking agencies that charge high fees, according to a post on the Xintian county police branch’s social media account on Tuesday.
